title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode a categorical variable, you create a binary column for each category. For example, if you have a column 'class' with values {First, Second, Third}, you will create three new columns: $$'class_{First'}$$, $$'class_{Second'}$$, and $$'class_{Third'}$$.

title: Intercept Term and One-Hot Encoding
text: Including an intercept term in a model with one-hot encoded variables can lead to linear dependence. This is because the intercept can be represented as a combination of the one-hot encoded columns.

title: Full Rank Matrix
text: A matrix is full rank if all its columns are linearly independent. If there is a linear dependence among the columns, the matrix is not full rank.

hintAnswer: Linear dependence due to one hot encoded columns with an intercept term
title: Identify the Linear Dependence
text: Consider the one-hot encoded columns and the intercept term. How might they be linearly dependent?
choices: Linear dependence due to one hot encoded columns with an intercept term
More features than data points (20 data points, $$21$$ features)
The nonlinear transformations create duplicate columns
The intercept term is always zero
The design matrix has more rows than columns
